newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns grain output could fall below '96 level.
newsitem.headline: China warns grain output could fall below '96 level.

text.p: China on Monday warned that its grain output this year could fall below last year's record harvest because backward farming techniques meant that main growing areas were still at the mercy of the ravages of nature.
China's bumper harvest of 480 million tonnes in 1996 had surpassed expectations because of exceptionally good weather, the official Xinhua news agency said.

But officials attending a session of the National People's Congress, or parliament, said China's annual grain output had hit seven peaks since 1949 and that continued record crops were not guaranteed.
"Each bumper harvest was followed by a steep drop in output, seriously affecting the national economy," Xinhua quoted Lu Xueyi, a parliamentary deputy from the eastern province of Jiangsu, as saying.

The northeastern province of Heilongjiang, the breadbasket of China, produced a record 30.5 million tonnes of grain last year, Xinhua quoted Yue Qifeng, provincial Communist Party secretary, as saying.
However, "the province still lacks sound basic agricultural facilities and agricultural production still relies considerably on natural conditions," Xinhua quoted Yue as telling the meeting.
Parliamentarians had called for more market-oriented reforms for the sector, which consists of millions of tiny and inefficient family-run plots, Xinhua said.

"With a large population but with limited arable land and frequent natural disasters, China cannot afford to neglect agricultural production at any time," Premier Li Peng told parliament earlier this month.
